questions.question: rem is relative to:
questions.explanation: rem = root em. Scaling html font-size resizes all rem-based dimensions consistently.

questions.question: em in font-size is relative to:
questions.explanation: When set on font-size, em references the parent's font-size. (In other properties, em references the element's own font-size.)

questions.question: vw means:
questions.explanation: vw = viewport width unit; 100vw = full width. vh is height. Great for fluid type/layout.

questions.question: A pitfall of 100vw is:

options.text: It includes the vertical scrollbar width, causing horizontal overflow

questions.explanation: 100vw counts the scrollbar, so a 100vw element can be slightly wider than the visible area → horizontal scroll. Use max-width:100% or 100% where possible.

questions.question: % is relative to:
questions.explanation: Percentage widths are relative to the parent's width; heights to parent's height (when defined).

questions.question: vmin / vmax are relative to:

options.text: The smaller / larger of the viewport width and height

questions.explanation: vmin = 1% of the smaller viewport dimension; vmax = 1% of the larger. Useful for square/full-bleed elements.

questions.question: Why prefer rem for spacing/typography in a scalable system?

options.text: A single root size change scales the whole UI predictably (no em compounding)

questions.explanation: rem avoids the compounding problem of nested em, so resizing the root scales everything uniformly.

questions.question: ch unit equals the width of:

options.text: The '0' (zero) glyph of the element's font

questions.explanation: ch is the advance width of '0'; handy for sizing inputs/paragraphs to a character count (e.g. max-width: 60ch).
